home.projectsDescription: Practical cases in critical systems, payments, messaging, observability, and AI automation, connecting technical decisions to operational impact.

projectCards.title: Statement 2.0 • Swap
projectCards.description: Redesign of the statement flow with Kotlin and MongoDB, replacing a fragile ETL with a consistent model, clear contracts, and query-oriented data design.
projectCards.problem: BalanceHistory 1.0 depended on ETL, had poor synchronization, and often returned inconsistent data for statement and balance queries — a direct risk for a financial operation.
projectCards.solution: I worked on MongoDB modeling guided by the PACELC criterion, redefined service contracts, and handled race conditions between asynchronous processes, in Kotlin, backed by MongoDB Atlas training.
projectCards.impact: Fewer balance-history inconsistencies, more predictable financial queries, and a flow less coupled to fragile ETL processes, with persistence decisions justified by explicit trade-offs.
projectCards.role: Technical ownership of the flow: I modeled persistence, evolved service contracts, handled concurrency, and documented decisions for the team.

projectCards.title: Workers, Webhooks and Observability • Swap
projectCards.description: Diagnosis and evolution of the webhooks and notifications pipeline: telemetry per URL, realm and flow to expose bottlenecks that intuition could not see.
projectCards.problem: The system processed high message volume, but there was no visibility into which URLs, realms and queues concentrated load or how Oban worker configuration impacted delivery. Incidents were investigated blind.
projectCards.solution: I instrumented telemetry to count messages by URL, realm, and application flow, correlating metrics with Oban worker behavior and making visible where the queue accumulated and why.
projectCards.impact: In a documented incident, diagnosis dropped from days to about 3 hours: the root cause (workers with no priority configured) became obvious and the fix was data-driven. The path became a technical article.
projectCards.role: End-to-end ownership: I defined the needed metrics, instrumented the application, investigated the incident, proposed the fix, and documented the process in an article.

projectCards.title: AI-Powered Triage Automation • Swap
projectCards.description: Automation flow with n8n, AI, and Slack to classify requests, trigger development workflows, and remove manual work from operations.
projectCards.alt: Workflow diagram with connected nodes representing automation and integrations
projectCards.problem: Demands such as fixes, refactors, and helpers arrived continuously and had to be analyzed, classified, and routed manually before any development.
projectCards.solution: I built an automation with n8n integrated with LLMs and Slack that interprets the request context, classifies, routes to the correct flow, and triggers the right steps (fix, refactor, analysis), keeping traceability.
projectCards.impact: Fewer manual steps in triage and a standardized intake. It reinforced the need for observable, resilient automations with human fallback for ambiguous cases.
projectCards.role: I designed and implemented the end-to-end flow: AI classification, n8n orchestration, notifications, and integration with the development workflow.

projectCards.title: Real-Time Communication Platform • Alertrack
projectCards.description: Backend and frontend for a communication platform, bots, and real-time automations, including building the build system from scratch and sustaining over 500k active users.
projectCards.problem: A communication platform with high user volume needed services resilient to message spikes, webhook integrations with external APIs, and a build/deploy that did not rely on fragile manual processes.
projectCards.solution: I developed Elixir services using native concurrency, webhooks, and cache to absorb message spikes; integrated APIs, webhooks, and on-premise servers; and built the build system from scratch, supporting deploys, QA, monitoring, and operations.
projectCards.impact: Platform sustained for over 500k active users, with message spikes absorbed through concurrency and cache, and reproducible deploy pipelines that reduced release friction and operational incidents.
projectCards.role: I worked from development to infrastructure: Elixir services, build system, integrations, technical support, and high-volume environment operations.

projectCards.title: RememberMe • In-Memory Cache for Elixir
projectCards.description: Open source in-memory cache library (ETS) built to reduce database load under high concurrency, published on Hex.
projectCards.problem: A service received ~2,000 concurrent requests querying the same dataset; repetitive access overloaded the database and increased latency.
projectCards.solution: I implemented an in-memory cache library based on ETS, with simple invalidation and an ergonomic API, published as an open source package on Hex for reuse.
projectCards.impact: Lower database pressure, reduced read latency under concurrency, and a reusable caching pattern for other Elixir applications.
projectCards.role: I identified the bottleneck, defined the strategy, implemented, documented, and published the package.
